title: Adversarial re-probe of the V0.0 forge+mission artifacts — 6 attacks, all re-run against the live seam

consumed.seam_probed_at: commit 9ef3250a (loop/v0.0-mission worktree, detached) — the exact code the mission validated

attacks.target: Contract drift — forge '§4 signatures verbatim' claim + mission goalpost a_ports_contract
attacks.evidence: Re-ran all 5 port_contract probes against the live seam at 9ef3250a: every contract_holds=true; param NAMES verbatim (SafetyPort.evaluate_path=[agent_id,path_history_hash,recent_actions,proposed_action,scene_state_digest], MemoryPort.query_and_filter=[relation_keys,task_context_tokens], LedgerPort.author_precommit=[claim_predicate,probability,world_ref], StagePort.compose_sanitized_stage=[stage_identifier]); return_annotation=PortResult on all four. NITS: (1) inspect.signature shows ALL param type annotations are absent (<none>) in the seam — blueprint docs/THE_LOOP_v5.1.md:104-146 declares agent_id:str, recent_actions:List[Dict[str,Any]], etc. The probe (harness/loop/probes.py:146-147) checks names only, so 'verbatim' holds for names, not the full annotated signature. (2) PortResult.payload is defaulted (=None) in the seam vs REQUIRED in the blueprint (docs/THE_LOOP_v5.1.md:106); PortResult('SUCCESS') constructs in the seam but would TypeError under the blueprint. Both are relaxations — no blueprint-following caller breaks (annotations are unenforced; callers bind by name).
attacks.fix: For claim precision: say '§4 param names verbatim' not 'signatures verbatim'; optionally add the blueprint's type annotations to the seam. No functional fix required.

attacks.target: Mapper smuggling — mission goalpost b_mapper_truth_table (unevaluable_blocks=true) vs mapper.py docstring principle
attacks.evidence: All 27 truth-table rows re-verified: ALLOW iff all True; any False or None -> BLOCK; non-bool -> TypeError per spec (mapper.py:32-33). OUTSIDE THE FORGE'S ROWS: GATE_POLICY([]) -> ALLOW (command: `python -c ... GATE_POLICY([])`, returned 'ALLOW'). mapper.py:18-26 documents 'any None -> BLOCK (unevaluable blocks: absent evidence is a block, never a pass-by-omission)' — an empty predicate set is the purest form of absent evidence, yet passes by omission. The function's stated principle and its empty boundary disagree. Not reachable in V0.0 (recipe never calls GATE_POLICY; probes/tests pass only 3-element combos), and GATE_POLICY is spec-only, never a live gate (ports.py docstring), so no production smuggling path.
attacks.fix: Treat an empty predicates iterable as BLOCK (absent evidence blocks), or amend the docstring to bound the contract to non-empty iterables.

attacks.target: Closure honesty — mission goalpost e_closure_rate (closure_rate=1.0, zero HIT/MISS, all EXPOSED)
attacks.evidence: probe_closure_rate(5) re-run: closure_rate=1.0, HIT=0, MISS=0, EXPOSED=5/5, goalpost_holds=true. Honest: settlement genuinely UNAVAILABLE (Hanish absent, ports.py:175-181), so every verdict is EXPOSED — no fabricated settlement/verdict. NIT: the metric itself is tautological — probes.py:293-294 computes closure_rate = sum(all verdict counts)/turns, and run_recipe always assigns every turn a verdict, so closure_rate is 1.0 by construction for ANY recipe run and can never fail. The discriminating signal is the underlying counts (HIT=0, MISS=0, EXPOSED=5), which are real and verified. 'closure_rate = 1.0' as a goalpost is decorative, not a test.
attacks.fix: State the goalpost as 'zero HIT/MISS and all turns EXPOSED' (the verifiable claim); treat closure_rate=1.0 as derived, or compute it as EXPOSED/(HIT+MISS+EXPOSED) so it can actually fail.

Forge commit 9ef3250a touches only python/synapse/loop/ports.py + tests/test_loop_contracts.py (git show --name-only) — territory claim holds. All 5 JSON artifacts parse cleanly.
